- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.40 or lower) — model tends to ignore downside risk.
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes — model overreacts to recent highs and fails to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days) — true price often rises faster than model suggests.
- When sentiment turns positive mid-period, model often overshoots and fails to adjust downward — especially if sentiment was negative prior.
- Model consistently overestimates in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon — likely due to momentum bias or failure to account for near-term volatility.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overcorrects downward — suggesting it underweights sentiment signals.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds too much upward bias even after 3–5 consecutive price increases.
- Forecast should be adjusted downward if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days — model often ignores sentiment shifts too late.
